fixes.explanation: True! God says Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), “…must burn the incense perpetually before the LORD for the generations to come.” The text has Aaron burning it every morning when he tends the lamps, and again when he sets up the lamps at twilight (Exodus 30:7-8). Generations to come? That's a longer run than any batch I've ever baked.

Drinking, huh? I love the thinking, baker, but nobody's filling a cup at this basin. God says the water is for Aaron and his sons “…to wash their hands and feet.” It's a washing basin, plain and simple. Hands and feet get the water, and no one is lining up with a thirsty throat.

That one's true, friend. God says to consecrate these things “…so that they will be most holy. Whatever touches them shall be holy.” Read that again slowly, because it says a lot. Being set apart is serious business here, and God is the one who sets it.

Judges, huh? I see where you're going, baker, but that's not the word in this verse. God tells Moses to anoint Aaron and his sons and “…consecrate them to serve Me as priests.” Judges never shows up in it. Priests is the word that fills the blank, and Aaron and his sons are the ones set apart for it.
